correctness.rationale: With hub color zero, any boundary in the rim between zero and nonzero forces the nonzero endpoint to switch (two zero neighbors). A nonunanimous fixed rim therefore avoids zero. With the remaining two colors, a rim vertex fails to retain its color exactly at an isolated singleton; when its two rim neighbors have different colors all three votes differ and it retains its color. The hub retains its absent opinion exactly when the rim is balanced. This covers the triangle rim and gives the binary comparison as well. Mark a start of a run of one fixed rim color: there are n indexed choices and two independent compositions of m into r parts ≥2, and every indexed word is marked r ways, even when it is rotationally periodic. For the sharp prefactor, the pair transfer trace counts each indexed cyclic word once. Setting z=e^t and λ=e^{t/2}u gives u^4−2cosh(t/2)u^3+u^2−1=0. At t=0 its primitive Perron root is φ, u'(0)=0 and u''(0)/φ=φ²/(4√5)=(5+3√5)/40. The loops at 00 and 11 force any common peripheral edge phase to be both 1 and z, so z=1 is the only Fourier saddle. Near zero the central phase cancels the first derivative of log λ; the remaining Gaussian integral has amplitude one because the trace gives coefficient one to the simple eigenvalue. Away from zero the compact Fourier arcs have a uniform spectral gap. This establishes the even central coefficient and excludes a spurious second lattice factor. Fresh direct open-neighbor enumeration at all n=3,...,10 reproduced 3,15,3,21,3,39,3,93. Exact finite sums at n=40 to 400 were also compared numerically with the limiting expression; neither test replaces the proof.

value.rationale: The wheel is a basic network where the hub makes local rim stability compete with a single global population constraint. The structural characterization and exact count explain the change from three equilibria to exponentially many on the even subsequence, including a hub that remains fixed despite no supporting rim neighbors. The sharp prefactor quantifies the cost of balance. This is useful as a fixed-point benchmark, not as a conclusion about convergence or basin sizes.
